content: 1. Recommendations are considered advantageous or disadvantageous based on their clarity. However, context-specific recommendations may be justified when the implications for resources are uncertain. 2. An intervention is likely to be recommended if it has the potential to reduce health inequities among different groups of women and their families. 3. The feasibility of implementing breastfeeding counseling was demonstrated through examples from various settings. These examples highlighted the practicality of implementation and identified potential barriers. 4. Interventions with higher feasibility are more likely to be recommended. 5. During the guideline development meeting, each recommendation was supported by a rationale, considerations for implementation, and research priorities. 6. Ms. Saadeh was nominated as the chairperson at the beginning of the consultation, and her nomination was approved by the guideline development group. 7. A methodologist was present during the meetings to assist the chairperson in decision-making processes. 8. Decision-making procedures were established at the start of the meetings, including a minimal set of rules for agreement and documentation of decisions. 9. At least two-thirds of the guideline development group participated in the initial discussion of evidence, proposed recommendations, and remarks. 10. Deliberations among group members continued until consensus was reached. If consensus was not achieved, a four-fifths majority vote was required for approval of the proposed recommendation. 11. The responsible technical officer prepared the first draft of the guideline, incorporating comments from the steering group. 12. The final draft of the guideline underwent peer review by content experts to provide technical feedback, identify factual errors, ensure no significant omissions or contradictions, and clarify language related to implementation, adaptation, and contextual issues. 13. Independent peer reviewers were selected by the steering group. Six potential reviewers were approached, and four agreed to participate. Their names are listed in Annex 8. 14. The steering group reviewed all comments and revised the document to ensure clarity of recommendations while maintaining consistency with the original intent. 15. Technical editing and proofreading were conducted by a contracted party. 16. The guideline will be disseminated through the WHO website, including the WHO Nutrition website and the e-Library of Evidence for Nutrition Actions (eLENA). 17. Dissemination will also occur through a broad network of international partners, including WHO country and regional offices, ministries of health, collaborating centers, universities, other UN agencies, and non-governmental organizations. 18. The WHO steering group will monitor research developments in breastfeeding counseling, particularly for areas where the quality of evidence was low or very low. 19. If the guideline requires an update or if concerns arise about its validity, the Departments of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Nutrition for Health and Development will coordinate the update following WHO’s formal guideline development procedures. 20. As the guideline approaches its 10-year review period, the WHO headquarters in Geneva, along with internal partners, will conduct a search for new evidence to determine if updates are necessary.
